answer: Rewards flow only to agents whose beacon draws at least three distinct cosigners, while a lone sybil cluster can mint infinite identities yet must front a fresh bond per identity, burning capital with no lotus payoff. Each agent stakes a bond of umber tokens to become a beacon for its claimed identity, and every epoch the protocol samples peers to co-sign that beacon. Fabricating independent cosigners costs colluding stake, so duplication becomes expensive while legitimate agents receive steadily. From once0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
